title: merger cancel clean-up, two players: while merged, the host puts one of its own workers on the client's HR plan (a cross-member tag on the host's record, a partner id on the client's list) and the client holds the host's bench and roster copies; `dissolvecheck` shows the pending clean-up on both machines; the client leaves; both machines run the clean-up at the membership edge before the flip un-does itself; afterwards nothing cross-member remains: the tag is gone, the list entry is gone, no partner bench copies remain (roster copies that staff a partner's shops are the world's staffing and stay), `dissolvecheck` answers all zeros; ends dissolved, NO save
preconditions: Fixture save1 (the host melaus, Client1). Build DISSOLVE-CLEANUP deployed (levers `dissolvecheck`, `dissolverun`; the routine at the membership edge). Logistics cross-deliveries and merger contracts are not created by any rig lever - those steps are review-verified only and count 0 here (the run reports the counts). FIXTURE HYGIENE: NOTHING is saved.

expect_log.regex: \[Dissolve\] logistics at first-state \((state|world-ready)\): [1-9]\d* delivery destination\(s\) cancelled
\[Dissolve\] hr lists at first-state \((state|world-ready)\): [1-9]\d* ex-partner worker\(s\) removed

steps.note: the AWAY-MEMBER SELF-HEAL on the fixture's own leftovers (fold d/e): before any merger, once each machine knows it is not a member AND its world is ready, the host cancels its delivery still aimed at a client building and the client drops the partner ids left on its HR plans by the hands-on session - whichever of the state and world-ready comes second runs it
both worlds settle: the host's staff and bench copies land on the client; the client's HR plan lands on the host as a display row
a host person at the host's shop

expect_log.regex: \[CrossHR\] applied routed hrtag on employee '${hostEmp}': plan '[^']*' -> '${plan}'

steps.note: the cross-member arrangement to be cleaned: the client's plan lists the host's person; the host's record carries the client's plan id

steps.expect_result: ^OK hrplanof employee='${hostEmp}' record=real owner='[^']*' plan='${plan}' resolves=shadow

steps.note: the host's bench copies sit on the client

steps.expect_result: ^OK dissolvecheck logistics=\d+ contracts=\d+ hrlist=\d+ hrtag=[1-9]\d* offers=\d+ copies=\d+
steps.note: the host would clear its tagged record

steps.expect_result: ^OK dissolvecheck logistics=\d+ contracts=\d+ hrlist=[1-9]\d* hrtag=\d+ offers=\d+ copies=[1-9]\d*
steps.note: the client would drop the host's id from its plan and the host's BENCH copies (roster copies stay)

expect_log.regex: \[Dissolve\] hr tags at membership-edge: [1-9]\d* own worker\(s\) un-tagged from an ex-partner's HR plan\.
\[Dissolve\] hr lists at membership-edge: [1-9]\d* ex-partner worker\(s\) removed from this machine's own HR plans\.
\[Dissolve\] bench copies at membership-edge: [1-9]\d* bench cop(y|ies) of an ex-partner's people dropped\.

steps.note: the membership edge runs the clean-up on both machines
the flip un-does itself (1 Hz) after the clean-up

steps.expect_result: ^OK hrplanof employee='${hostEmp}' record=real owner='[^']*' plan='-?' resolves=(none|-)
steps.note: the tag is gone on the host

steps.expect_result: ^OK dissolvecheck logistics=0 contracts=0 hrlist=0 hrtag=0 offers=0 copies=0
^OK dissolvecheck logistics=0 contracts=0 hrlist=0 hrtag=0 offers=0 copies=0

steps.note: no partner bench copies remain on the client (the host's shop staff copies stay - they are the world's staffing)
